continuation_context.key_insight: exist_transfer_upgrade with Nat.rec on k, arity n universally quantified. Statement: from depth-(k+1) (n+1)-var agreement, depth-(k+1) (n+2)-var existential transfer. Inductive step (succ k ih): (1) extract hex from h_agree's quantifier condition, (2) find z' via hex using nf_characteristic at depth k, (3) h_full := nf_agreement_from_shared_nf gives depth-k (n+2)-var agreement, (4) atoms via atom_agreement_from_nf, (5) quant via (ih (n+1) M (Fin.cons z envM) N (Fin.cons z' envN) h_full chi_sub).symm. The .symm handles the Iff direction mismatch between goal (N iff M) and IH (M iff N).
continuation_context.proven_mechanism: The inductive step works because: the quantifier condition of depth-(k+2) agreement gives depth-(k+1) existential transfer (hex). Finding z' via hex using the depth-(k+1) characteristic gives depth-(k+1) (n+2)-var agreement (h_full). The IH applied at n+1 with h_full converts depth-(k+1) (n+2)-var agreement to depth-(k+1) (n+3)-var existential transfer. This is exactly the quantifier condition of the depth-(k+2) sub_nf.
continuation_context.base_case_analysis: At k=0: depth-1 agreement. The quant condition gives depth-0 existential transfer. Finding z' gives depth-0 (n+2)-var agreement. But the quantifier of depth-1 sub_nf requires depth-0 (n+3)-var existential transfer at [z,envM]/[z',envN]. Depth-0 means purely atomic. The existential introduces a NEW variable whose atoms (predicates + orders to all n+2 env elements) need matching. This is structurally impossible without model-specific guarantees (e.g., Prior-UZ: any 1-var type in any interval is realized).
